What is money and why do we use it?

Great question! Money is anything that people generally accept for buying and selling goods and services. In Nigeria, our money is the naira and kobo. We use money because it makes trade easy. Long ago, people used trade by barter, exchanging goods directly, like swapping a basket of yam for a goat. But barter was difficult: what if the goat owner did not want yam? Money solved this problem, because everybody accepts it. With money you can buy food, pay school fees, pay for transport, and save for the future. Money is a very useful servant!

What are the denominations of the naira?

Good question! Denominations are the different values of our money. Nigerian banknotes come in 5 naira, 10 naira, 20 naira, 50 naira, 100 naira, 200 naira, 500 naira and 1,000 naira. Each note has its own colour and shows the face of an important Nigerian, like Alhaji Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa on the 5 naira note. We also have coins of 50 kobo, 1 naira and 2 naira, though they are rarely used today. Remember, 100 kobo make 1 naira. Knowing your denominations helps you count money and check your change correctly. Well done!

What is a bank and what does it do?

Lovely question! A bank is a place where people keep their money safely. Instead of hiding money under the bed, where it can be stolen or burnt, people open accounts and save their money in the bank. Banks do many things: they keep money safe, they allow you to withdraw your money when you need it, they lend money to people who want to start or grow a business, and they help people send money to others far away. Banks also give ATM cards for easy payment. The Central Bank of Nigeria watches over all the other banks. Banks keep our money working safely!

Why should I save money instead of spending it all?

Wonderful question! Saving means keeping part of your money for the future instead of spending everything now. Saving is wise for many reasons. It prepares you for emergencies, like when you suddenly need a new exercise book. It helps you buy bigger things later: saving 50 naira weekly gives you 200 naira in a month. It teaches discipline and patience, values that will help you all your life. It also gives you peace of mind, because you are not stranded when needs arise. You can save in a kolo savings box or, with your parents, in a bank. Start saving small today!

What is the difference between needs and wants?

Very smart question! Needs are things we must have to live and stay healthy: food, clean water, clothes, shelter, education and medicine. Wants are things that are nice to have but we can live without: sweets, biscuits, toys, fancy shoes and video games. When spending money, wise people take care of needs first before wants. If you have 200 naira and you need an exercise book for 120 naira, buy the book before thinking of biscuits. Learning to separate needs from wants helps you spend wisely and save more. Ask yourself before buying: is this a need or a want?

How do people earn money?

Great question! People earn money by working honestly. Some people are employed and receive salaries: teachers, nurses, doctors, police officers, bankers and civil servants. Some people run their own businesses: traders selling in the market, farmers selling crops like yam and maize, tailors sewing clothes, mechanics repairing cars, and barbers cutting hair. Some people earn through skills and talents, like footballers, musicians and artists. What is common to all of them is honest hard work; money earned through stealing or cheating brings trouble and shame. Study hard now, learn skills, and you will earn well in future!

What are the modern ways of paying for things without cash?

Good observation question! Today, Nigerians pay for many things without carrying cash. Bank transfers move money from one account to another using a phone app or USSD codes. ATM or debit cards allow you to pay in shops using a POS machine, the small device you see with traders and POS agents. Mobile money and payment apps let people send and receive money quickly. These methods are fast and safer than carrying plenty of cash, but they must be used carefully: never share your PIN or password with anyone. Cashless payment is part of our modern financial system!

How should I take care of naira notes?

Very responsible question! The naira is a national symbol, so we must handle it with respect and care. Do not squeeze, tear or rumple naira notes; keep them flat and neat in a purse or wallet. Do not write or draw on the notes. Do not spray or stamp on naira at parties; it is actually against the law to abuse the naira. Keep money away from water, oil and dirty places. Torn and dirty notes have to be replaced, which costs the country money. Handling the naira well shows you are a patriotic Nigerian. Take care of our money!
